newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament fails to pass peace pact.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament fails to pass peace pact.

text.p: Parliament in Belarus failed late on Friday to approve a peace deal brokered by Russia intended to end deputies' standoff with hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.

Lukashenko left the chamber and told reporters he would consult the Russian leadership and his government and decide his next move on Saturday. Parliament adjourned until Tuesday after failing four times to approve the agreement during the evening.
The pact, mediated in all-night talks by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, was designed to defuse a conflict over a referendum on Sunday designed by Lukashenko to increase his powers.
Lukashenko threatened to renege on the deal, signed at dawn on Friday, unless the deputies passed it by a two-thirds majority by the end of the day.
But less than 100 of the 199 deputies in the parliament gave it their support.

Many members saw the pact, under which Lukashenko agreed the referendum would only be advisory, as a sellout. The deadlock in parliament appeared to leave the agreement, hailed by Moscow as a diplomatic triumph, on the verge of collapse.
